I am 44 years old and have farmed in Quzhou County my whole life. I only went to primary school, but I know my 7 mu of land well. My husband works part-time in town, so most of the farming falls on me and my mother-in-law. 

This year I will stick with what I always do: winter wheat and summer corn on the same 7 mu. I already planted the wheat last October after ploughing the field. I bought improved seeds from the county supply shop — they are not the cheapest, but they grow better than the seeds I keep myself. Last year I used about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu and got roughly 460 kg per mu. My neighbor Lao Zhang used less fertilizer and his crop looked thinner than mine, so I will stay at 15 kg nitrogen, plus about 6 kg phosphorus and 5 kg potassium. The soil here is decent but needs these nutrients. I will irrigate three times: once in spring when the wheat turns green, once at jointing, and once at filling. Water is expensive now with the electric meters on the tube wells, so three times is what I can afford. I will spray pesticides twice for weeds and insects.

After wheat harvest in early June, I have less than a week to plant corn. I will use hybrid seeds — everyone does now because the yield is so much better. I will rotary-till quickly after harvesting the wheat; there is no time for deep ploughing. For the corn I will apply about 17 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate two or three times depending on the rain, and spray pesticides twice. I expect about 520 kg per mu from the corn.

I thought about cotton because some villagers grow it, but cotton needs too much hand-picking labor and the price is unpredictable. Wheat and corn are safer. The grain station always buys them, and I need the flour for my family and the corn to feed our pigs. With my son's school fees this year, I cannot afford a bad crop, so I will not try anything new.
